trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.verdict: made money but lagged the index
narrative.headline: Made money but lagged the index: +5.06% total return vs +14.41% for the index, +1.24pp residual after beta, -18.5% max drawdown, 0.36% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at +5.06%, profitable but 9.35pp behind the S&P 500's +14.41%.
The momentum premium this participant is built to harvest was live (+4.98% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
Of the +5.06% total, about +3.83pp is explained by carrying beta 0.27 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.02); the residual +1.24pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
TSLA contributed +11,794 USD (233% of net P&L) across 9 closed trades; CVNA was the biggest drag at -18,024 USD.
Execution cost 359 USD (0.36% of starting capital, 1.2 bp per fill, 1.3 bp of the 2,835,984 USD traded). 80% of that was spread/depth/impact and 20% was explicit fees and rebates.
50 closed round trips, 50.0% winners, profit factor 1.08, average winner +2,836 vs average loser -2,627 USD, median holding 15 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 249 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 1269 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).

Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -18.51% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-04-10, recovered 2026-04-23. Average gross exposure 51% of starting capital, peak leverage 1.95x.
Daily returns were -0.42 skewed with excess kurtosis +5.09; historical 95% VaR -2.48%/day with CVaR -4.26%/day. Worst single session -8.82%, best +6.33%.

Standing limitations of this simulation that apply to this participant regardless of the regime: PROXY DATA LIMITATION: no earnings calendar or EPS surprise series is available offline, so the entry uses a price/volume proxy rather than a real announcement (flagged as IR-07)

None of the failure modes declared in the strategy spec fired in this window.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 75.5pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @DriftRider_PEAD (Drift Rider) ran the "post-event drift" archetype. Declared thesis: Markets digest a large information shock over days, not seconds. When a name moves more than 8% in five sessions on at least twice its normal volume, the move continues in the same direction for weeks - the drift that earnings announcement research documents. Entry: 5-session absolute return > 8%; 20-session average volume on the event day >= 2.0x the 63-session average; Go with the direction of the move, up to 5 names, ranked by |move|. Exit: Hold 15 sessions then exit; Exit early if the move retraces more than 60%. Sizing: equal 35% of equity per name = up to 175% gross. Leverage: up to 1.75x gross. Cadence: daily scan, horizon 15 sessions. Aggression 4/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Concentrates into the strongest information event in the universe and refuses to take profit early.
